By Aaron Bailey

Delta Air Lines is inching closer and closer to announcing a new nonstop service to Asia. Rumours have been swirling for weeks that the SkyTeam carrier will debut in Singapore Changi Airport (SIN), with the airline likely to begin flying from 

Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) or Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA).

Credit: Minh K Tran | Shutterstock

 At this time, it remains unclear whether Delta will pick Singapore to be served from Los Angeles or Seattle. Both airports are key to the airline's West Coast network and Asia-Pacific growth. When Delta adds services to Singapore, it will face stiff competition from one other major full-service airline, Singapore Airlines, which flies the route up to 11 times a week. United Airlines is the only current US operator to Singapore, serving the destination nonstop from San Francisco International Airport (SFO).

ultimate.title: Delta Air Lines' Major New 18-Hour Ultra-Long Nonstop Route: See Flights Now
ultimate.snippet:
By Aaron Bailey 

 Published Oct 13, 2026, 5:00 PM EDT

...

Delta Air Lines is inching closer and closer to announcing a new nonstop service to Asia. Rumours have been swirling for weeks that the SkyTeam carrier will debut in Singapore Changi Airport (SIN), with the airline likely to begin flying from 

Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) or Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). 

For Delta, Singapore is not a new destination, with the airline previously serving the Lion City via Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT) up until 2019. This time, the route will be served nonstop, with the Airbus A350-900. This aircraft type is the largest in the airline's current fleet, with the A350-1000 set to begin flying for the airline next year. 

## Will Delta Serve Singapore From Los Angeles Or Seattle? 

Credit: Minh K Tran | Shutterstock

 At this time, it remains unclear whether Delta will pick Singapore to be served from Los Angeles or Seattle. Both airports are key to the airline's West Coast network and Asia-Pacific growth. Los Angeles has been instrumental in recent years with network expansion for the carrier, such as the airline's announcements of nonstop flights to Hong Kong (HKG) and Manila (MNL).

When Delta adds services to Singapore, it will face stiff competition from one other major full-service airline, Singapore Airlines, which flies the route up to 11 times a week. Delta would likely serve Singapore up to three times a week, offering less than a third of Singapore Airlines' capacity. United Airlines is the only current US operator to Singapore, serving the destination nonstop from San Francisco International Airport (SFO).
